prompt: A polling firm wants a $95\%$ confidence interval for a proportion with margin of error at most $0.03$. Using $z^* = 1.96$ and the conservative guess $p^* = 0.5$, what is the smallest sample size that works?
explanation: The margin of error is $z^* \sqrt{p^*(1-p^*)/n}$. Requiring it to be at most $0.03$ gives $n \ge p^*(1-p^*) (z^*/0.03)^2$.
Sample sizes are whole numbers and we need AT LEAST this much, so round up: $n = 1068$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why round up and why 0.5?
steps: $n = 1067$ gives ME slightly more than $0.03$ — fails. $1068$ is the first that works.
$p^* = 0.5$ makes $p^*(1-p^*)$ as large as possible ($0.25$), so the sample is big enough no matter what the true $p$ turns out to be.
That is why national polls so often use "about 1,000 people": it buys a $\pm 3\%$ margin at $95\%$.
